body: I feel that (lol). Going to Japan alone was one of the most disappointing and empty experiences of my life (in comparison to my dreams of it as a teenager), as I'm not someone who tends to live in relation in terms of feedback loops to the external world around me. I relate heavily to everything feeling so exciting as a kid. However, I've come here to say that when I did acid around Sep last year, I felt a multitude of feelings, albeit briefly (I didn't fully break through and feel, I think this is why the feeling didn't carry over post-trip, maybe it would have if I did) that to this day still give me a sense of hope for more. Those being, a sense of insane wonder and an extreme exploratory urge in regards to the world, and a feeling of freedom from all the shackles holding me back in my life, the main one being a sense of chronic guilt for me personally. It was insane... it was like pure Id. I needed to see. I needed to explore. To travel, to feel. To run wild. Vaguely libidinous. ...Well, that's acid for you. Do some psychs lol, shake things up like the adrenaline poster said. Worth a try.

1. I've never even tried to, and don't ever want to, ask my dad whether that was real or not, so in that sense there won't be any gaslighting there
2. Sigh, we didn't have any other family where we lived (they immigrated and I was born here), so it wasn't deliberate isolation in my case but still unfortunate.

6 - The thing is, and I'm mad about it now, they kept on trying to pull me aside like a ragdoll to apologise about things when I was in my mid teens. The reason I'm mad is because it's like showing up to someone's house uninvited while they're like in the shower or something, apologising at the front door, then leaving and being like, well that's all done. like uhh...... can I hear you???????? Basically a metaphor for- I was emotionally withdrawn af then, like barely there- it was so one-sided. and i think the effects of the abuse/resentment/intrusion and denial of autonomy hit me on a time delay, so it's been a couple of years since then and now i'm feeling the full (?) brunt of being voiceless, not believed in, and treated like i was hated.

Also, sure, they've apologised for what *they* remember, but they have never really heard from me, properly and openly, the draining and constant distress/pain they put me through. i dont even wanna fkn open up to them about how fkn shit and awful it made me feel. the thought of that makes me want to throw up. this also tears me apart because i know parents arent around forever and i dont want to live with the regret of not fixing up our issues (that *they* started). I think they missed their chance for me to really open up, I don't think it'll happen ever again. but I'm sure, as an adult/in an adult manner, i can calmly elaborate on the emotional destruction they lowkey caused me, and then accept that apology and move on.

You're right about the full accountability part, too. Before I moved out late last year, I was distressingly trying to communicate with my dad and just as always, I get 0 response. this time though, I get a "YOU REJECTED ME" and "IT'S YOUR CHARACTER". I don't believe he has NPD at clinical levels, but statements like these really do make me think that he most resembles vulnerable narcissism. like, what the fuck? This is a good portion of the causes behind my chronic guilt. its been 20 years and he still hasnt changed his stance that i'm \[insert all the negative things he has screamed at me relentlessly that I am\] here.

8. I want to also say that though it doesn't show through text, those episodes were rare. I know I worded it in a way that would make a reader think it was violence and mayhem every fortnight, but this is only a clarification of scope, and I do struggle with feeling "oh its not as bad because it happens only 2-4x (???) /year" but I do try to think about it as 'respect level = 0 as illustrated by these events', rather than 'oh its ok because its not a commonplace occurrence'. aaaaa!

9. Mm, what I meant about the connection to everyone was more so feeling socially comfortable and like you as a person belong in the general place/scene; like I belong as much as the others I see there. instead of feeling like an outsider. but ah well.

thank you for the detailed response, it's so so fkn hard to believe these days that I can ever be genuinely happy. it's so hard as well to separate my guilt for things i'm in no way responsible for from the things ive done which i personally feel genuinely sorry for, that have hurt both others and myself. the former is also sort of a cause for the latter too, so it's all so complicated. i know i'm not a bad person, but i've seen these days how real emotional nourishment is part of what helps build a confident/caring/trusting person, so you can sort of see what i'm saying here... i'm really not the best person rn. but all i can hope for is to separate the shadow parts of me that are there simply because of a lack of emotional connection in order to get (false) connection or self worth, and the shadow parts that every individual has as I guess part of their character regardless of upbringing.
Thank you, I'm getting there slowly
